newsitem.title: GERMANY: Report says German govt, opposition plan tax talks.
newsitem.headline: Report says German govt, opposition plan tax talks.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition and the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) plan to resume talks on tax reform soon and could strike a deal that includes raising value added tax, a German newspaper said on Saturday.

In an advance copy of a report to appear on Sunday, the weekly Welt am Sonntag newspaper cited unnamed SPD officials saying that a deal on tax reform with Kohl's centre-right government would be reached "in the very near future".
The officials also said that a compromise with the government was being worked out that would include a rise in value added tax by one point to 16 percent that could take effect as soon as July.
"Big things are on the horizon," the paper quoted one official as saying.

The government would be willing to bring forward its income tax reform to 1998, a year earlier than planned, in exchange for the SPD support to slash the top rate to 39 percent from 53 and the entry rate to 15 percent from 25.9 percent.
The plan also called for lowering supplementary wage costs and cutting unemployment insurance payments to 5.5 percent of gross salaries and wages from 6.5 percent now.
In addition to raising value added tax, petrol taxes could also be increased in order to pay for the tax cuts, the report said.

A spokeswoman for Finance Minister Theo Waigel dismissed the report. "The government coalition is always ready to talk," Barbara Eckrich told reporters on the sidelines of a meeting of Eurpean Union finance ministers in the Netherlands.
"But because of the blockade of the SPD there have been no further talks. That is why all of the details mentioned (in the Welt report) are pure speculation," she added.

SPD spokeswoman Dagmar Wiebusch said in a statement that the party is prepared to talk with the government about tax reform measures that could ease the burden on families, but dismissed details in Welt as "not suited for this purpose".
